201115485_9901be4d.text: The pontine nucleus locus coeruleus (LC) contains the majority-about 10,000-15,000 neurons on each side in humans and 1,500 in rodents-of central noradrenergic neurons that project to a wide variety of targets including cerebellum, prefrontal cortex and hippocampus (Berridge et al., 2003)(Moore et al., 1979)(Swanson, 1976)

201115485_fb3ee02c.text: .Electrophysiological studies of LC neurons have identified several characteristic functional features such as low‐frequency pacemaker activity with broad action potentials, transient high‐frequency burst discharges in response to salient stimuli and an apparently homogeneous inhibition of firing by activation of somatodendritic α2 autoreceptors (α2AR)

201115485_ebfcbbe2.text: .Using fluorescent beads‐mediated retrograde tracing in adult C57Bl6/N mice, we compared the anatomical distributions and functional in vitro properties of identified LC neurons projecting either to medial prefrontal cortex, hippocampus or cerebellum. The functional in vitro analysis of LC neurons confirmed their mostly uniform functional properties regarding action potential generation and pacemaker firing. However, we identified significant differences in tonic and evoked α2AR‐mediated responses. While hippocampal‐projecting LC neurons were partially inhibited by endogenous levels of norepinephrine and almost completely silenced by application of saturating concentrations of the α2 agonist clonidine, prefrontal‐projecting LC neurons were not affected by endogenous levels of norepinephrine and only partially inhibited by saturating concentrations of clonidine.
